slides.title: What robusta changes in espresso
slides.subtitle: Crema, body, flavor and one myth.

slides.title: Crema: robusta's signature
slides.body: Crema is the light-brown foam on top of an espresso. Robusta usually makes more of it than arabica. That is one reason some espresso blends include a little.
slides.highlight: More robusta usually means more foam.

slides.title: Body: weight on your tongue
slides.body: Body is how heavy a coffee feels in your mouth. A small share of good robusta can add body to a blend, which also helps an espresso stand up to milk.
slides.highlight: Arabica for nuance, robusta for weight.

slides.myth: Robusta is always the cheap, bad coffee.
slides.truth: Quality depends on the farm and the processing, for both species. Well-grown robusta can add body and crema, and some roasters use it on purpose.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Read your espresso bag: does it say 100% arabica or mention robusta? Then taste for sweetness, body and crema.

slides.title: Nuance or body?
slides.body: Arabica is sweeter and more complex. Robusta adds crema and weight. Many blends mix both.
